subject: Discovery recap + head-to-head validation plan for DataSwitch evaluation
snippet: Recap of yesterday's discovery, prioritized decision criteria, proposed head-to-head tests and timelines.
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Ward <amelia@dataswitch.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap + head-to-head validation plan for DataSwitch evaluation

Hi Amelia — great to meet yesterday, thanks for the time. Below is a concise recap of what we heard, the decision criteria you emphasized, and a proposed set of head-to-head tests to validate parity across vendors. I’ve attached a brief proposal and a suggested PoC schedule.

Key pain points you described
- High inference unit cost at scale (current cost >$0.15/token equivalized for customer-facing flows)
- Latency tail causing UI jank for live search/autocomplete (spikes >200ms under load)
- Data residency + auditability requirements for logs and keys (SOC2 + country controls)

Primary goals for the next 90 days
1) Demonstrate predictable 95th/99th latency under a realistic workload (search/autocomplete + long-form assist)
2) Show 2x cost improvement vs current baseline with acceptable quality delta
3) Validate private deployment path (VPC + KMS) and audit traceability

Decision criteria (as prioritized on call)
- Latency SLOs (95th/99th)
- Cost per 1k tokens (unit economics)
- Security/compliance: KMS, audit logs, network controls
- Ops burden: rollout, tracing, and model swap mechanics
- Quality regressions vs incumbent (sample evals)

Proposed head-to-head tests (what we recommend running in the bake-off)
A. Latency tail test: sustained 100 req/s mixed-size traffic for 2 hours capturing P50/P95/P99 and cold-start tails
B. Throughput cost test: sustained throughput with throughput-to-cost mapping (token accounting)
C. Prefix caching & KV replay: evaluate cache hit uplift across typical sessions
D. Streaming & partial-output quality: measure time-to-first-token for streaming scenarios
E. Security & deployment proof: deploy Redwood Private in a VPC trial and demonstrate KMS key rotation + audit log export
F. Quality probes: standardized prompt set (you shared examples) to measure semantic parity; we’ll include automatic evals and human review for edge cases

Next steps we propose
- Confirm procurement contact (CC Ben) and contract timeline
- Redwood to run an initial 48-hour latency/throughput quick-test (no install) to sanity-check baselines — deliverables: quick-test report + log export
- If quick-test meets gating thresholds, spin up a week-long head-to-head PoC with full logging and SLO dashboards

Proposed timeline
Week 0: finalize scope & procurement paperwork
Week 1: quick sanity tests (48 hrs) + shared metrics dashboard
Weeks 2–3: head-to-head PoC execution
End Week 3: readout + decision rubric scorecard

Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-proposal-v1.pdf (proposal + measurement rubric)

Open items for you
- Confirm procurement contact & target contract signature date
- Share any hard constraints for data residency or IP retention we should bake into the Private run

I’ll follow up with a short runbook and the head-to-head matrix we’d like to use for scoring. Appreciate any immediate clarifications — happy to jump on a 20-min call if that helps.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0182

[Attachment: redwood-bakeoff-proposal-v1.pdf (pdf)]

From: Amelia Ward <amelia@dataswitch.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Chu <bchu@dataswitch.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + head-to-head validation plan for DataSwitch evaluation

Hi Marissa — thanks for the thoughtful recap, this aligns with our notes. A few quick clarifications and asks:

1) Procurement: please loop Ben (copied) for contract timing — we typically need procurement sign-off within 3 weeks if commercial looks aligned.
2) Priority weighting: latency (real-time search) is our #1 gating criterion, cost improvement is second, and private deployment + auditability are third. If a vendor fails #1 we won’t proceed.
3) On the Private run: what’s the minimum infra footprint we should expect? Are we able to run a pilot in our AWS account (VPC peering) or would Redwood-hosted Private in our region be necessary?

Open Qs for the head-to-head tests
- Can you include an embeddings-specific probe? We use embeddings for retrieval; we need to see embedding vector stability and performance under concurrent batch loads.
- For streaming, we need time-to-first-token measured separately from full-response latency.

I attached our internal decision criteria workbook — it has the rubric the procurement team will use.

If you can send the proposed head-to-head matrix and an explicit list of logs/artifacts you will provide (ship logs, metrics, traces, KV cache dumps), that will help us engage SRE and security.

Thanks — happy to sync Thursday if that works.

Regards,
Amelia Ward
VP Product, DataSwitch
amelia@dataswitch.io

[Attachment: dataswitch-decision-criteria.xlsx (xlsx)]

Hi Amelia / Ben — great — thanks for the worksheet, that helps. Per your ask I’ve attached our head-to-head scoring matrix and a short runbook that lists the exact artifacts we’ll collect for each test. High level notes below plus an explicit asks list for SRE/security.

What we’ll measure (summary)
- Latency: P50/P95/P99 and time-to-first-token for streaming
- Cost: measured tokens consumed + infra cost mapped to per-1k-token unit economics
- Embeddings: similarity stability and throughput under concurrent batch jobs
- Deployment proof: KMS key usage, audit export, network policy demo

Proposed 3-week execution plan (expanded)
- Week 0 (this week): scope & procurement sign-off, share runbook + credentials for test harness (short-lived IAM role)
- Week 1: Quick sanity run (48 hours) across vendors to validate traffic profile and baseline metrics
- Week 2: Full head-to-head, vendor A/B comparisons with scoring matrix across your rubric
- Week 3: Buffer for ops work, handoff, and commercial negotiations

Artifacts we will deliver (explicit)
- Raw request/response logs (anonymized)
- Aggregated latency histograms and tail-event traces
- Token accounting and cost math workbook
- Embedding vectors & sample retrieval tests (CSV)
- Runbook with timeline and incident contacts

Security / SRE asks for you
1) Provide an IAM role or temporary credentials for the test harness (scoped to the test bucket)
2) Confirm whether logs can be exported to your S3/GCS bucket during the trial
3) Any IP/EULA clauses we should pre-clear for embeddings export

Attachments: headtohead-matrix.csv (scoring matrix), runbook-outline.md (artifacts + commands)

Proposed immediate asks
- Amelia / Ben: confirm procurement timeline and whether we can start the quick sanity run this Friday (Dec 3)
- DataSwitch SRE: confirm preferred artifact export location and access method
- Redwood SE (Rishi): prepare quantized & non-quantized config we’ll use for cost/quality comparison (Rishi will reach out with specifics)

Happy to set a 20-minute handoff with your SRE and our solutions team (Grace and Rishi) — feel free to propose times.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

[Attachments: headtohead-matrix.csv (csv), runbook-outline.md (text)]
